reasons: The cited text is a genuine deviation: Article IV.I permits a seven-year extension at the Licensor's sole option, with no Customer consent, no non-renewal notice window and no cap on renewal fees — squarely in the rule's walk-away zone (automatic/unilateral multi-year renewals).

The redline implements the preferred position precisely: renewal only by mutual written agreement, renewal term reduced to successive 12-month periods, and renewal fee increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

The edit is surgical in substance — only the offending second sentence is replaced; the termination-for-breach and payment-retention sentences and sub-clauses II and III are preserved verbatim, and the new language is internally consistent with Articles IV.II and III.

The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' check is a phrasing artifact, not a defect: under a mutual-written-agreement renewal there is no auto-renewal to opt out of, so no notice-window figure is required.
The 0.718 changed-character ratio is advisory and overstated here; the rule requires rewriting the renewal sentence, and no unrelated text was touched.

The comment is accurate, correctly attributed to the playbook, states what changed and why in two sentences, and offers the fallback (12-month auto-renewal with 60-day opt-out, 5% cap) without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.
